We're seeing a sudden spike in client-side 429 responses and 2-3x tail latency on calls to /v1/generate from our production service in us-west-2 starting ~08:45 PDT. This is affecting our triage and billing flows — SLOs are breached for a subset of our customers.

- 429s concentrated on routes hitting model: redwood/opt-l7-large (mostly long-context requests)
- Overall throughput to your endpoint dropped ~40% despite no change in our traffic pattern
- We did a quick check on our side and there were no deploys or traffic bursts at that time

We need confirmation this is not a product-side regression. Can you triage and advise next steps ASAP? We're preparing an incident bridge.

Thanks,

Quick update from diagnostics (initial findings):

What I see:
- Around 08:40 PDT a config push changed the global "burst_window_ms" default from 5000 -> 500 for the runtime rate limiter (this was intended for an internal experiment on test clusters).
- The rollout config mistakenly inherited into the production tenant policy because the policy template id matched a deprecated alias; our template inheritance code did not block scope when alias collision occurred.
- Result: effective token bucket refill for certain dedicated tenants dropped by ~90% for long-sequence model routes; that explains the spike in 429s + downstream throughput collapse.

Immediate mitigation (recommended):
1) Apply emergency override to Acme Health tenant: set tenant_rate_limit_override = "burst_window_ms:5000,burst_tokens:1200" via admin API (I will run).
2) Roll back the unintended template change in the config store and trigger a controlled canary to validate.
3) Deploy a hotfix to the template resolution code path to prevent alias collisions (low-risk patch).

I attached the diagnostic snippet showing token-bucket counters and the config diff: diagnostic-ratepolicy.log.

I'll apply the override now and report back within 10 minutes.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: RESOLVED: Rate-limit template inheritance issue fixed — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sarah —

Short summary: root cause was a config-template alias collision that caused a lower burst window to be applied to dedicated tenant policies during a config rollout on 2026-05-18 08:39 PDT. Jonas applied an operator override for Acme (burst_window_ms=5000, burst_tokens=1200) and we rolled back the template change.

What we did:
- Emergency override applied at 11:38 PDT on 2026-05-18; metrics show 98% of traffic restored and 429s reduced to baseline within ~7 minutes. See attached post-fix throughput graph (postfix_throughput.png).
- Patch to template-resolution code merged and scheduled for staged rollout tonight (will not change tenant config; it prevents future alias collisions).
- 48-hour override window set; we intend to make the change permanent only after regression testing and a short canary.
- We've scheduled a postmortem and a customer-facing incident report for Friday 2026-05-22.

Apology and compensation:
We recognize the impact this had on Acme's production traffic. We'll include a credit in the incident report calculation if the SLO breach is confirmed. I'm also available to join your engineering review to walk through the fix and the prevention plan.

Attach: post-fix throughput graph + diagnostic log (diagnostic-ratepolicy.log).

Best,
Dylan Brooks
